chapter: Gangsters, records, women musicians and the blues
title: First awareness of gangsters at the Burnham Inn; how they treated artists
summary: Burnham was where she first knew she was working for gangsters; they protected artists, paid well and ran most clubs through fronts, and she will say only good things about them.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Now, do you remember when you first came into contact with gangsters? When were you first aware of gangsters in the clubs?

I was first aware of gangsters in the clubs, it was at Burnham, Illinois. There was a club out there called the Burnham Inn. B-u-r-n-h-a-m, Burnham Inn. It was in Burnham, Illinois. I used to have to take a train to get out there. And when I went out -- I was working out there and making a whole lot of money, and I know that's the first time I knew that I was working with gangsters. And then I was naive again, because this fellow that -- fellow that killed somebody and got away and they finally caught him. What was his name? Charley something. I don't remember his last name. It'll come to me. But anyway, this -- at the Burnham Inn, I know, one night I was singing. I told you about that, though, didn't I?
Yeah. When the lights went out and when they went back on the man was laying there dead.
Uh-huh. Well, that's the first time that I really knew that I was working with gangsters.
But the gangsters generally -- my impression is that the gangsters --
They gave the artists a lot of money and they enjoyed them.
Nobody would bother us. And remember, ask me some more about gangsters, because when I worked in Nashville, Tennessee, ask me about that, hear?
But gangsters also hired artists, right? They ran some of the clubs.
Gangsters ran most of the clubs.
And had people fronting for them.
See? People used their names for them. But I can't swear that they did.
You know, I don't know, and I'm not going to get into that.
No, because they were all -- they were so good to me that I have absolutely nothing to say about them but something good. Nothing.
